verdict.rationale: NVIDIA documents a broad set of official SDKs that developers can build against on this GPU. These include the CUDA Toolkit (libraries, compiler, runtime, plus cuTile Python and CUDA Tile C++), the RTX Neural Shaders SDK, the Video Codec SDK, the PhysX SDK, the HPC SDK, the pip-installable Holoscan SDK, CUDA-X libraries such as cuML and cuDF, and an NGC catalog of SDKs. One community critic notes that this card's SM120 architecture lacks support in some major libraries tuned for SM100, a depth caveat rather than a contradiction. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of building against these SDKs on this card, and evidence of full library parity for SM120.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: The toolkit includes GPU-accelerated libraries, debugging and optimization tools, a C/C++ compiler, and a runtime library.
The RTX Neural Shaders SDK lets developers train shader data on an RTX PRO workstation and accelerate neural representations with NVIDIA Tensor Cores at runtime.
All you need to build AI—GPU-optimized containers, pretrained models, SDKs, and Helm charts—unified in one catalog for cloud, data-center, or edge.
